hook: Stop digging through bins for the thing in back

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands digging through a packed shelf bin, moving jars aside to reach something in the back corner
scenes.voiceover: If you're moving six things to reach the one in the back, this is for you.

scenes.visual_prompt: 10-inch lazy susan turntable being placed on a shelf, spice jars arranged on top
scenes.voiceover: A set of 4 non-skid turntables, 10 inches each, $24.99.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand spinning the turntable smoothly, items rotating into view without sliding off
scenes.voiceover: 4.7 stars across 6,190 reviews — and the non-skid base is why it stays put.

scenes.visual_prompt: Turntable placed inside a clear storage bin next to painter's tape labels being applied to the bin front
scenes.voiceover: Pair it with painter's tape labels and you've got a fully rotating, fully labeled system.

scenes.visual_prompt: Overlay text showing math: turntables $24.99 + labels $6-8 = under $35
scenes.on_screen_text: under $35 on top of your bins
scenes.voiceover: Under $35 total on top of the bins you already bought.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of pantry-adjacent basement shelf, turntables spinning into frame, fully labeled clear bins around them
scenes.on_screen_text: organized in 6 months, not just today
scenes.voiceover: This is what makes it stick past week one.

caption: A bin system without labels is just the same mess in clear plastic. These non-skid turntables ($24.99, 4.7 stars, 6,190 reviews) plus a $6 label kit solved the dig-through-everything problem for me. Full system at the link.
